title: Communicable diseases
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: toxin
items.clue: A poison that bacteria may produce.

items.label: measles
items.clue: A viral disease showing symptoms of fever and a red skin rash.

items.label: tobacco mosaic virus (TMV)
items.clue: A widespread plant pathogen affecting many species of plants including tomatoes.

items.label: vector
items.clue: An organism that carries a pathogen from one host to another without being the pathogen itself.

options.text: A bacterium that causes an infectious disease
A poison that damages tissues and makes us ill
A microorganism that lives inside the body cells
A microorganism that causes infectious disease

questions.explanation: Pathogens are microorganisms that cause infectious disease. They may be viruses, bacteria, protists or fungi, and may infect plants or animals.

questions.stem: How is the spread of salmonella food poisoning controlled in the UK?

options.text: People are vaccinated against salmonella
Poultry are vaccinated against salmonella
Poultry are treated with strong antibiotics
People are given painkillers to cure it

questions.explanation: Salmonella food poisoning is spread by bacteria ingested in food, and in the UK poultry are vaccinated against salmonella to control the spread.

questions.stem: Purple and black spots have appeared on the leaves of a rose bush in a garden. How is this disease most likely to reach the other rose bushes in the garden?

options.text: By insects moving between the plants
By direct contact between the leaves
By toxins spreading through the soil
By water or wind in the environment

questions.explanation: Rose black spot is a fungal disease that is spread in the environment by water or wind, so it can cross the gap between plants that never touch.

questions.stem: What kind of pathogen causes malaria?

options.text: A protist spread to humans by mosquitos
A bacterium spread to humans by mosquitos
A mosquito that bites and infects humans
A virus that reproduces in human cells

questions.explanation: The pathogens that cause malaria are protists, and the malarial protist has a life cycle that includes the mosquito.

questions.stem: Which of these is a non-specific defence system of the human body?

options.text: The nose produces antibodies to attack pathogens
The stomach produces acid that kills pathogens
Cilia in the trachea destroy trapped pathogens
White blood cells in the skin trap pathogens

questions.explanation: The stomach is one of the non-specific defence systems of the human body: it produces hydrochloric acid that kills pathogens in swallowed food and mucus.

questions.stem: A health agency wants to reduce the number of malaria cases in a region. Which approach should it use?

options.text: Treating infected people with antibiotics
Stopping mosquitos breeding and using nets
Vaccinating whole populations against it
Avoiding direct contact with infected people

questions.explanation: The spread of malaria is controlled by preventing the vectors, mosquitos, from breeding and by using mosquito nets to avoid being bitten.

questions.stem: Bacteria in the blood are releasing toxins. Which action of the white blood cells deals with those toxins?

options.text: The production of antibodies
The engulfing of the bacteria
The production of antitoxins
The production of stomach acid

questions.explanation: White blood cells help to defend against pathogens by antitoxin production, and antitoxins counteract the toxins that bacteria produce.

questions.stem: A pathogen gets past the body's non-specific defences and enters the body for the first time. What does the immune system do?

options.text: It produces toxins to kill the pathogen
It tries to destroy the invading pathogen
It develops resistance to the pathogen
It waits for a vaccination to be given

questions.explanation: If a pathogen enters the body the immune system tries to destroy the pathogen, using phagocytosis, antibody production and antitoxin production.
